settings.name_in_paper: Contextual linear bandit with linear constraints

Known safe action x_0 available in every A_t with known cost c_0 < tau
Regret is against the optimal feasible policy (distribution over actions) at each round
Mean rewards and costs in [0,1]; ||theta_*||, ||mu_*|| <= S
settings.definition_quote: In each round $t$, the agent is given an decision set $\mathcal A_t\subset{\mathbb R}^d$ from which it has to choose an action $x_t$. Upon taking action $x_t\in\mathcal A$, it observes a pair $(r_t,c_t)$, where $r_t=\langle x_t,\theta_*\rangle + \xi^r_t$ and $c_t=\langle x_t,\mu_*\rangle + \xi^c_t$ ... while satisfying the linear constraint $\mathbb E_{x\sim\pi_t}[\langle x,\mu_* \rangle]\leq \tau,\quad\forall t\in[T]$

unmapped: Each arm has a reward and a cost distribution with means in [0,1]; policy pi_t must satisfy expected cost <= tau each round
Arm 1 is a known safe arm with known cost c_bar_1 < tau
Regret is against the optimal feasible (mixed) policy
Noise model not explicitly stated; confidence widths sqrt(2 log(1/delta)/T_a) suggest 1-sub-Gaussian
settings.definition_quote: In the MAB setting, the action set consists of $K$ arms ... Each arm $a\in [K]$ has a reward and a cost distribution with means $\bar{r}_a,\bar{c}_a\in [0,1]$. ... while satisfying the linear constraint $\mathbb E_{a_t\sim\pi_t}[\bar{c}_{a_t}] \leq \tau,\;\forall t\in[T]$. Moreover, arm $1$ is assumed to be the known safe arm

symbols.c_0: known cost of the safe action x_0

conditions: safe action x_0 in every A_t with known cost c_0 < tau

source.label: theorem::main_theorem_linear
source.quote: Let $\alpha_c = 1$ and $\alpha_r = \frac{ 2+\tau-c_0}{\tau-c_0}$. Then, with probability at least $1-2\delta$, the regret of OPLB satisfies $\mathcal{R}_{\Pi}(T) \leq \frac{2L(\alpha_r+1)\beta_T(\delta, d)}{\sqrt{\lambda}}\sqrt{2T\log(1/\delta)} + (\alpha_r+1)\beta_T(\delta, d)\sqrt{2Td\log(1+\frac{TL^2}{\lambda})}$.

results.notes: Holds w.p. 1-2delta. Regret is constrained pseudo-regret w.r.t. optimal feasible policy, bounded with high probability. Order O~(d sqrt(T)/(tau-c_0)). Also policies are feasible w.h.p. (Proposition 2). Computational tractability is not claimed (paper says the optimization can be challenging).

symbols.c_bar_1: known mean cost of safe arm 1

conditions: arm 1 is a known safe arm with c_bar_1 < tau

source.label: theorem::contrained_MAB
source.quote: Let $\delta = 4KT\delta'$, $\alpha_c=1$, and $\alpha_r = 1+2/(\tau-\bar{c}_1)$. Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of OPB satisfies $\mathcal{R}_\Pi(T) \leq \big(1 + \frac{2}{\tau-\bar{c}_1}\big) \times \big(2\sqrt{2KT\log(4KT/\delta)} + 4\sqrt{T\log(2/\delta)\log(4KT/\delta)}\big).$

results.notes: Appendix Theorem 4 restates this with epsilon in place of delta. Comparator is the optimal feasible mixed policy. Noise model for arm distributions not stated explicitly. OPB is computationally efficient (LP solution with support <= 2).

symbols.gap_min: min_i (tau_i - c_bar_1^(i)), smallest slack of safe arm across constraints

conditions: learner knows c_bar_1^(i) < tau_i for all constraints i

source.quote: If $\epsilon \in(0,1)$, $ \alpha_c=1$ and $\alpha_r = \frac{2}{\min_i \tau_i-\bar{c}^{(i)}_1} + 1$, then with probability at least $1-\epsilon$, Algorithm \ref{alg::optimism_pessimism} satisfies the following regret guarantee: ...

results.notes: Probability 1-epsilon; epsilon here is a failure probability (paper's notation). Algorithm is multi-constraint extension of OPB.

conditions: unit-variance Gaussian rewards and costs with means in [0,1]^K

source.quote: Let $\tau, \bar{c}_1 \in (0,1)$, $K \geq 4$, and $B:=\max\left(\frac{1}{27}\sqrt{ (k-1) T}, \frac{1}{6(\tau - \bar{c}_1)^2} \right)$  and assume $T \geq \max(  K-1,24eB)$ ... Then for any algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ there is a pair of mean vectors $\bar{r}, \bar{c} \in [0,1]^K$ such that: $\mathcal{R}_\Pi(T, \mathcal{A}, \bar{r}, \bar{c}) \geq B$

results.notes: Minimax lower bound; regret quantity is the constrained (pseudo-)regret in expectation presumably. Proof somewhat informal.
